claim: Current channelrhodopsin-based optogenetic tools lack strict ion selectivity.
source: The application of current channelrhodopsin-based optogenetic tools is limited by the lack of strict ion selectivity and the inability to extend the spectra sensitivity into the near-infrared (NIR) tissue transmissible range.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a limitation of existing tools.

claim: Current channelrhodopsin-based optogenetic tools cannot extend spectral sensitivity into the near-infrared tissue transmissible range.
source: The application of current channelrhodopsin-based optogenetic tools is limited by the lack of strict ion selectivity and the inability to extend the spectra sensitivity into the near-infrared (NIR) tissue transmissible range.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a limitation of existing tools.

claim: Opto-CRAC is an NIR-stimulable optogenetic platform that selectively controls Ca2+ oscillations.
source: Here we present an NIR-stimulable optogenetic platform (termed 'Opto-CRAC') that selectively and remotely controls Ca2+ oscillations and Ca2+-responsive gene expression to regulate the function of non-excitable cells, including T lymphocytes, macrophages and dendritic cells.
evidence: This is the main claim of the study presented in the abstract.

claim: Opto-CRAC remotely controls Ca2+-responsive gene expression in non-excitable cells.
source: Here we present an NIR-stimulable optogenetic platform (termed 'Opto-CRAC') that selectively and remotely controls Ca2+ oscillations and Ca2+-responsive gene expression to regulate the function of non-excitable cells, including T lymphocytes, macrophages and dendritic cells.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of the Opto-CRAC system in the abstract.

claim: Opto-CRAC regulates the function of T lymphocytes, macrophages, and dendritic cells.
source: Here we present an NIR-stimulable optogenetic platform (termed 'Opto-CRAC') that selectively and remotely controls Ca2+ oscillations and Ca2+-responsive gene expression to regulate the function of non-excitable cells, including T lymphocytes, macrophages and dendritic cells.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of the Opto-CRAC system in the abstract.

claim: Coupling Opto-CRAC to upconversion nanoparticles shifts the optogenetic operation window from visible to NIR wavelengths.
source: When coupled to upconversion nanoparticles, the optogenetic operation window is shifted from the visible range to NIR wavelengths to enable wireless photoactivation of Ca2+-dependent signaling and optogenetic modulation of immunoinflammatory responses.
evidence: This is stated as a key feature of the system in the abstract.

claim: Opto-CRAC enables wireless photoactivation of Ca2+-dependent signaling when coupled to upconversion nanoparticles.
source: When coupled to upconversion nanoparticles, the optogenetic operation window is shifted from the visible range to NIR wavelengths to enable wireless photoactivation of Ca2+-dependent signaling and optogenetic modulation of immunoinflammatory responses.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of the UCNP-coupled system in the abstract.

claim: Opto-CRAC acts as a genetically-encoded 'photoactivatable adjuvant' in a mouse melanoma model using ovalbumin as surrogate tumor antigen.
source: In a mouse model of melanoma by using ovalbumin as surrogate tumor antigen, Opto-CRAC has been shown to act as a genetically-encoded 'photoactivatable adjuvant' to improve antigen-specific immune responses to specifically destruct tumor cells.
evidence: This is stated as a demonstrated application in the abstract.

claim: Opto-CRAC improves antigen-specific immune responses to specifically destruct tumor cells in a mouse melanoma model.
source: In a mouse model of melanoma by using ovalbumin as surrogate tumor antigen, Opto-CRAC has been shown to act as a genetically-encoded 'photoactivatable adjuvant' to improve antigen-specific immune responses to specifically destruct tumor cells.
evidence: This is stated as a demonstrated outcome in the abstract.

claim: Microbial opsin-based optogenetic technologies have been widely adopted to modulate neural activity.
source: Microbial opsin-based optogenetic technologies have been widely adopted to modulate neural activity (Fenno et al., 2011), but similar tools tailored for utilization in non-excitable tissues (e.g., the immune and hematopoietic system) are still limited.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: Optogenetic tools tailored for non-excitable tissues such as the immune and hematopoietic system are still limited.
source: Microbial opsin-based optogenetic technologies have been widely adopted to modulate neural activity (Fenno et al., 2011), but similar tools tailored for utilization in non-excitable tissues (e.g., the immune and hematopoietic system) are still limited.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in the field in the introduction.

claim: Channelrhodopsin-based optogenetic tools are limited by lack of ion selectivity.
source: The application of channelrhodopsin (ChR)-based optogenetic tools is limited by the lack of ion selectivity and the inability to extend the spectral sensitivity into the near-infrared (NIR) range (Fenno et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as a limitation with a citation in the introduction.

claim: Channelrhodopsin-based optogenetic tools cannot extend spectral sensitivity into the near-infrared range.
source: The application of channelrhodopsin (ChR)-based optogenetic tools is limited by the lack of ion selectivity and the inability to extend the spectral sensitivity into the near-infrared (NIR) range (Fenno et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as a limitation with a citation in the introduction.

claim: The CRAC channel is one of the most Ca2+-selective ion channels.
source: Here we present a tissue penetrable near infrared-stimulable optogenetic platform (termed 'Opto-CRAC') that can be used to reversibly photo-manipulate Ca2+ influx through one of the most Ca2+-selective ion channels, the Ca2+ release-activated Ca2+ (CRAC) channel, which is abundantly present in most non-excitable cells (Hogan et al., 2010; Prakriya and Lewis, 2015).
evidence: This is stated as a property of the CRAC channel with citations.

claim: The CRAC channel is abundantly present in most non-excitable cells.
source: Here we present a tissue penetrable near infrared-stimulable optogenetic platform (termed 'Opto-CRAC') that can be used to reversibly photo-manipulate Ca2+ influx through one of the most Ca2+-selective ion channels, the Ca2+ release-activated Ca2+ (CRAC) channel, which is abundantly present in most non-excitable cells (Hogan et al., 2010; Prakriya and Lewis, 2015).
evidence: This is stated as a property of the CRAC channel with citations.

claim: Opto-CRAC is based on engineering light sensitivity into the CRAC channel.
source: Our tool is based on the engineering of light sensitivity into the CRAC channel and its subsequent coupling to lanthanide-doped upconversion nanoparticles (UCNP), the latter of which act as nanotransducers to convert tissue penetrable NIR light into visible light emission (Shen et al., 2013; Chen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as the basis of the tool design in the introduction.

claim: Lanthanide-doped upconversion nanoparticles act as nanotransducers to convert tissue penetrable NIR light into visible light emission.
source: Our tool is based on the engineering of light sensitivity into the CRAC channel and its subsequent coupling to lanthanide-doped upconversion nanoparticles (UCNP), the latter of which act as nanotransducers to convert tissue penetrable NIR light into visible light emission (Shen et al., 2013; Chen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as a property of UCNPs with citations.

claim: Opto-CRAC tools can remotely control Ca2+ influx and generate repetitive Ca2+ oscillations.
source: We demonstrate that Opto-CRAC tools can be applied to remotely control Ca2+ influx and generate repetitive Ca2+ oscillations, photo-tune Ca2+-dependent gene expression, and modulate a myriad of Ca2+-dependent activities in cells of the immune system, including effector T cell activation, macrophage-mediated inflammasome activation, dendritic cells (DC) maturation and antigen presentation.
evidence: This is stated as a demonstrated capability in the introduction.

claim: Opto-CRAC tools can photo-tune Ca2+-dependent gene expression.
source: We demonstrate that Opto-CRAC tools can be applied to remotely control Ca2+ influx and generate repetitive Ca2+ oscillations, photo-tune Ca2+-dependent gene expression, and modulate a myriad of Ca2+-dependent activities in cells of the immune system, including effector T cell activation, macrophage-mediated inflammasome activation, dendritic cells (DC) maturation and antigen presentation.
evidence: This is stated as a demonstrated capability in the introduction.

claim: Opto-CRAC tools can modulate effector T cell activation.
source: We demonstrate that Opto-CRAC tools can be applied to remotely control Ca2+ influx and generate repetitive Ca2+ oscillations, photo-tune Ca2+-dependent gene expression, and modulate a myriad of Ca2+-dependent activities in cells of the immune system, including effector T cell activation, macrophage-mediated inflammasome activation, dendritic cells (DC) maturation and antigen presentation.
evidence: This is stated as a demonstrated capability in the introduction.

claim: Opto-CRAC tools can modulate macrophage-mediated inflammasome activation.
source: We demonstrate that Opto-CRAC tools can be applied to remotely control Ca2+ influx and generate repetitive Ca2+ oscillations, photo-tune Ca2+-dependent gene expression, and modulate a myriad of Ca2+-dependent activities in cells of the immune system, including effector T cell activation, macrophage-mediated inflammasome activation, dendritic cells (DC) maturation and antigen presentation.
evidence: This is stated as a demonstrated capability in the introduction.

claim: Opto-CRAC tools can modulate dendritic cell maturation and antigen presentation.
source: We demonstrate that Opto-CRAC tools can be applied to remotely control Ca2+ influx and generate repetitive Ca2+ oscillations, photo-tune Ca2+-dependent gene expression, and modulate a myriad of Ca2+-dependent activities in cells of the immune system, including effector T cell activation, macrophage-mediated inflammasome activation, dendritic cells (DC) maturation and antigen presentation.
evidence: This is stated as a demonstrated capability in the introduction.

claim: T cell receptor engagement triggers a cascade of signaling events that elicit Ca2+ influx through the CRAC channel following antigen presentation.
source: Following antigen presentation, T cell receptor (TCR) engagement triggers a cascade of signaling events in T lymphocytes that elicit the influx of extracellular Ca2+ through the CRAC channel, a classic example of store operated Ca2+ entry (SOCE) (Hogan et al., 2010; Prakriya and Lewis, 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: The CRAC channel is a classic example of store operated Ca2+ entry (SOCE).
source: Following antigen presentation, T cell receptor (TCR) engagement triggers a cascade of signaling events in T lymphocytes that elicit the influx of extracellular Ca2+ through the CRAC channel, a classic example of store operated Ca2+ entry (SOCE) (Hogan et al., 2010; Prakriya and Lewis, 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Store depletion induced Ca2+ influx through CRAC channels activates calcineurin.
source: Store depletion induced Ca2+ influx through CRAC channels further activates calcineurin, a downstream Ca2+-dependent phosphatase that dephosphorylates the master transcriptional regulator NFAT (nuclear factor of activated T cells) and subsequently causes NFAT nuclear translocation (Müller and Rao, 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: Calcineurin is a Ca2+-dependent phosphatase that dephosphorylates NFAT.
source: Store depletion induced Ca2+ influx through CRAC channels further activates calcineurin, a downstream Ca2+-dependent phosphatase that dephosphorylates the master transcriptional regulator NFAT (nuclear factor of activated T cells) and subsequently causes NFAT nuclear translocation (Müller and Rao, 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: Calcineurin dephosphorylation of NFAT causes NFAT nuclear translocation.
source: Store depletion induced Ca2+ influx through CRAC channels further activates calcineurin, a downstream Ca2+-dependent phosphatase that dephosphorylates the master transcriptional regulator NFAT (nuclear factor of activated T cells) and subsequently causes NFAT nuclear translocation (Müller and Rao, 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: NFAT cooperates with AP-1 to turn on genes characteristic of a productive immune response in the presence of the co-stimulatory pathway.
source: In the presence of the co-stimulatory pathway, which activates the activator protein 1 (AP-1), NFAT cooperates with AP-1 to turn on genes (e.g., IL-2 and IFN-γ) that are characteristic of a productive immune response (Müller and Rao, 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: IL-2 and IFN-γ are genes characteristic of a productive immune response.
source: In the presence of the co-stimulatory pathway, which activates the activator protein 1 (AP-1), NFAT cooperates with AP-1 to turn on genes (e.g., IL-2 and IFN-γ) that are characteristic of a productive immune response (Müller and Rao, 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: Light sensitivity was installed into STIM1 by fusing STIM1-CT fragments with the LOV2 domain of Avena sativa phototropin 1.
source: To enable light control over the Ca2+/NFAT pathway, we set out to install light sensitivity into STIM1 by fusing a handful of STIM1-CT fragments with the genetically-encoded photoswitch LOV2 (light, oxygen, voltage) domain (residues 404–546) of Avena sativa phototropin 1 (Christie et al., 1999; Harper, 2003; Yao et al., 2008; Wu et al., 2009) (Figure 1a and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as the design strategy with citations.

claim: STIM1-CT fragments expressed alone are capable of eliciting varying degrees of constitutive activation of ORAI1 channels.
source: When expressed alone, these STIM1-CT fragments are capable of eliciting varying degrees of constitutive activation of ORAI1 channels to mediate Ca2+ entry from the extracellular space to the cytosol (Yuan et al., 2009; Park et al., 2009; Zhou et al., 2010a; Soboloff et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: In the dark, the C-terminal Jα helix docks to the LOV2 domain and keeps the ORAI1-activating STIM1-CT fragments quiescent.
source: In the dark, the C-terminal Jα helix docks to the LOV2 domain (Harper, 2003; Yao et al., 2008; Wu et al., 2009) and keeps the ORAI1-activating STIM1-CT fragments quiescent.
evidence: This is stated as the mechanism of the dark state with citations.

claim: Upon blue light illumination, photoexcitation generates a covalent adduct between LOV2 residue C450 and the cofactor FMN.
source: Upon blue light illumination, photoexcitation generates a covalent adduct between LOV2 residue C450 and the cofactor FMN (Figure 1—figure supplement 1d), thereby promoting the undocking and unwinding of the Jα helix to expose the STIM1-CT fragments.
evidence: This is stated as the mechanism of photoactivation and referenced to a figure.

claim: Blue light illumination promotes the undocking and unwinding of the Jα helix to expose the STIM1-CT fragments.
source: Upon blue light illumination, photoexcitation generates a covalent adduct between LOV2 residue C450 and the cofactor FMN (Figure 1—figure supplement 1d), thereby promoting the undocking and unwinding of the Jα helix to expose the STIM1-CT fragments.
evidence: This is stated as the mechanism of photoactivation.

claim: Unleashed STIM1-CT fragments move toward the plasma membrane to directly engage and activate ORAI1 Ca2+ channels.
source: Unleashed STIM1-CT fragments further move toward the plasma membrane to directly engage and activate ORAI1 Ca2+ channels (Figure 1a,b).
evidence: This is stated as the mechanism of channel activation and referenced to figures.

claim: LOVSoc showed no discernible dark activity and exhibited the highest dynamic range in evoking light-inducible Ca2+ influx.
source: After an initial screen of approximately 100 constructs using NFAT nuclear translocation and Ca2+ influx as readouts, we decided to use the LOV2-STIM1336-486 chimera (designated as 'LOVSoc') in our following experiments because it showed no discernible dark activity and exhibited the highest dynamic range in terms of evoking light-inducible Ca2+ influx (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a,b).
evidence: This is stated as the result of screening experiments with reference to figures.

claim: LOVSoc underwent rapid translocation between the cytosol and the PM in response to blue light illumination with t1/2,on = 6.8 ± 2.3 s and t1/2,off = 28.7 ± 6.5 s.
source: When expressed as an mCherry-tagged fusion protein in HEK293-ORAI1 stable cells, LOVSoc underwent rapid translocation between the cytosol and the PM in response to blue light illumination (t1/2,on = 6.8 ± 2.3 s; t1/2,off = 28.7 ± 6.5 s; Figure 1b and Video 1).
evidence: This is stated as experimental data with specific kinetic values and referenced to figures and video.

claim: The light-dependent translocation of LOVSoc could be readily reversed by switching the light off and repeated multiple times without significant loss in magnitude of response.
source: This process could be readily reversed by switching the light off, and could be repeated multiple times without significant loss in the magnitude of response.
evidence: This is stated as an observed property of the system.

claim: The light-dependent association between LOVSoc and ORAI1 or ORAI1-CT was confirmed by pulldown assay and coimmunoprecipitation assays.
source: The light-dependent association between LOVSoc and ORAI1 or ORAI1 C-terminus (ORAI1-CT) was further confirmed by a pulldown assay using purified recombinant proteins and by coimmunoprecipitation assays (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated as experimental validation with reference to a figure.

claim: The degree of Ca2+ influx in cells expressing LOVSoc could be tuned by varying the light power densities.
source: In mammalian cells expressing LOVSoc, the degree of Ca2+ influx could be tuned by varying the light power densities (Figure 1—figure supplement 3a).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation with reference to a figure.

claim: LOVSoc triggered elevation of cytosolic Ca2+ concentrations to approximately 500–800 nM in a dozen mammalian cell types after photostimulation for 1 min at 40 μW/mm2 at 470 nm.
source: After photostimulation for 1 min with a power density of 40 μW/mm2 at 470 nm, LOVSoc triggered significant yet varied elevation of cytosolic Ca2+ concentrations to approximately 500–800 nM in a dozen of mammalian cell types derived from various non-excitable tissues (Figure 1—figure supplement 3b), likely owing to the varied endogenous levels of ORAI proteins among the tested cells.
evidence: This is stated as experimental data with reference to a figure.

claim: The varied elevation of cytosolic Ca2+ concentrations among cell types is likely owing to varied endogenous levels of ORAI proteins.
source: After photostimulation for 1 min with a power density of 40 μW/mm2 at 470 nm, LOVSoc triggered significant yet varied elevation of cytosolic Ca2+ concentrations to approximately 500–800 nM in a dozen of mammalian cell types derived from various non-excitable tissues (Figure 1—figure supplement 3b), likely owing to the varied endogenous levels of ORAI proteins among the tested cells.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the observed variation.

claim: The half-life time of the cytosolic Ca2+ rise in response to light stimulation ranged from 23 s to 36 s depending on the Ca2+ indicator used.
source: Depending on the kinetic properties of the Ca2+ indicators used, the half-life time of the cytosolic Ca2+ rise in response to light stimulation ranged from 23 s to 36 s.
evidence: This is stated as experimental data.

claim: After switching off the light, the cytosolic Ca2+ signal decayed with a half-life time of approximately 25–35 s.
source: After switching off the light, the cytosolic Ca2+ signal decayed with a half-life time of approximately 25–35 s (Figure 1—figure supplement 3f).
evidence: This is stated as experimental data with reference to a figure.

claim: The time scale of LOVSoc-mediated Ca2+ influx is largely in agreement with the time scale of SOCE under physiological stimulation.
source: These values are largely in agreement with the time scale of SOCE under physiological stimulation (Hogan et al., 2010; Prakriya and Lewis, 2015; Soboloff et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison to established knowledge with citations.

claim: Following light stimulation, HEK293 cells transfected with LOVSoc developed a typical inward rectifying current characteristic of the CRAC channel.
source: Following light stimulation, HEK293 cell transfected with LOVSoc developed a typical inward rectifying current, which is characteristic of the CRAC channel and distinct from the greater outward currents of non-selective cation channels such as TRPC (Prakriya and Lewis, 2015).
evidence: This is stated as experimental data with a citation.

claim: Substitution of extracellular Na+ by NMDG+ did not alter the amplitude or overall shape of the LOVSoc-mediated photoactivatable CRAC current.
source: Substitution of the most abundant extracellular cation Na+ by a non-permeant ion NMDG+ did not alter the amplitude or overall shape of the CRAC current, implying that Na+ has negligible contribution to LOVSoc- mediated photoactivatable Ca2+-selective CRAC currents.
evidence: This is stated as experimental data.

claim: Na+ has negligible contribution to LOVSoc-mediated photoactivatable Ca2+-selective CRAC currents.
source: Substitution of the most abundant extracellular cation Na+ by a non-permeant ion NMDG+ did not alter the amplitude or overall shape of the CRAC current, implying that Na+ has negligible contribution to LOVSoc- mediated photoactivatable Ca2+-selective CRAC currents.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the experimental data.

claim: Prolonged interpulse interval was largely accompanied by a decrease in the nuclear accumulation of NFAT.
source: As shown in Figure 1f prolonged interpulse interval was largely accompanied by a decrease in the nuclear accumulation of NFAT.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation with reference to a figure.

claim: Higher Ca2+ oscillation frequencies tend to increase the ability to activate NFAT.
source: This observation agrees well with previous reports showing that higher Ca2+ oscillation frequencies, or faster repetitive Ca2+ pulses, tend to increase the ability to activate NFAT (Lewis et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated as agreement with established knowledge with a citation.

claim: Light illumination led to a robust increase in NFAT-driven luciferase gene expression in HeLa cells in the presence of PMA.
source: In the presence of the co-stimulatory pathway (mimicked by the addition of the pleiotropic PKC activator PMA), light illumination led to a robust increase in luciferase gene expression (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is stated as experimental data with reference to a figure.

claim: A decrease in the light pulse frequency caused a reduction in the efficiency of Ca2+/NFAT-driven luciferase expression.
source: A decrease in the light pulse frequency also caused a reduction in the efficiency of Ca2+/NFAT-driven luciferase expression (Figure 1f).
evidence: This is stated as experimental data with reference to a figure.

claim: Light stimulation led to robust production of insulin in cells transfected with LOVSoc but not in those without LOVSoc expression.
source: Upon light stimulation, we observed a robust production of insulin in cells transfected with LOVSoc, but not in those without LOVSoc expression (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is stated as experimental data with reference to a figure.

claim: Light stimulation remarkably boosted cytokine production by over 15–30 fold in CD4+ T cells transduced with mCh-LOVSoc in the presence of PMA.
source: Again, in the presence of PMA, light stimulation faithfully mimicked ionomycin-induced effects on the Ca2+/NFAT pathway and remarkably boosted the cytokine production by over 15–30 fold in CD4+ T cells transduced with mCh-LOVSoc.
evidence: This is stated as experimental data.

claim: Control cells transduced with the mock retrovirus failed to exhibit light-dependent production of cytokines.
source: By contrast, control cells transduced with the mock retrovirus failed to exhibit light-dependent production of cytokines (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as experimental data with reference to a figure.

claim: Intracellular Ca2+ immobilization in macrophage is critical for the activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome.
source: In addition to its well-established role in driving effector T cell activation, intracellular Ca2+ immobilization in macrophage is critical for the activation of the NLRP3 (nucleotide-binding domain, leucine-rich-repeat-containing family, pyrin domain-containing 3) inflammasome (Murakami et al., 2012; Lee et al., 2012; Horng, 2014), which is accompanied by the release of processed caspase-1 (p20 subunit) and the proinflammatory cytokine IL-1β into culture supernatants (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations and reference to a figure.

claim: NLRP3 inflammasome activation is accompanied by the release of processed caspase-1 (p20 subunit) and IL-1β into culture supernatants.
source: In addition to its well-established role in driving effector T cell activation, intracellular Ca2+ immobilization in macrophage is critical for the activation of the NLRP3 (nucleotide-binding domain, leucine-rich-repeat-containing family, pyrin domain-containing 3) inflammasome (Murakami et al., 2012; Lee et al., 2012; Horng, 2014), which is accompanied by the release of processed caspase-1 (p20 subunit) and the proinflammatory cytokine IL-1β into culture supernatants (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations and reference to a figure.

claim: Photostimulation at 5 or 50 μW/mm2 led to a light intensity-dependent boost in the production of IL-1β and processed caspase-1 in LPS-primed THP1-derived macrophages in the presence of nigericin.
source: Following photostimulation at 5 or 50 μW/mm2, we observed a notable light intensity-dependent boost in the production of IL-1β and processed caspase -1 (p20 subunit) in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-primed THP1-derived macrophages in the presence of a commonly used inflammasome inducer nigericin (Figure 2c), thus confirming the feasibility of harnessing the power of light to amplify macrophage-mediated inflammatory responses ex vivo.
evidence: This is stated as experimental data with reference to a figure.

claim: The synthesized UCNPs displayed a sharp emission peak centered around 470 nm when excited at 980 nm.
source: When excited at 980 nm, the synthesized UCNPs displayed a sharp emission peak centered around 470 nm (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is stated as experimental data with reference to a figure.

claim: UCNPs were able to cause photoactivation of recombinant LOV2 proteins following NIR light stimulation.
source: Like direct blue light illumination, UCNPs were able to cause photoactivation of recombinant LOV2 proteins, as reflected by the absorbance changes following NIR light stimulation and the subsequent recovery to the dark state (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is stated as experimental data with reference to a figure.

claim: In HeLa cells expressing mCh-ORAI1-StrepTag, there was remarkable local accumulation of UCNPs-Stv on the plasma membrane.
source: In HeLa cells expressing mCh-ORAI1-StrepTag, we detected remarkable local accumulation of UCNPs-Stv on the plasma membrane (Figure 3c), confirming the cell-specific targeting of functionalized nanoparticles.
evidence: This is stated as experimental data with reference to a figure.

claim: Within 20 s of NIR light stimulation, transfected HeLa cells exhibited a significant increase in GCaMP6s fluorescence indicating a rapid rise in intracellular Ca2+ concentration.
source: Within 20 s, transfected HeLa cells exhibited a significant increase in GCaMP6s fluorescence, indicating a rapid rise in the intracellular Ca2+ concentration that was evoked by NIR light (Figure 3d).
evidence: This is stated as experimental data with reference to a figure.

claim: Cells incubated with control NIR-to-green UCNPs did not show discernible changes in GCaMP6s signal upon NIR light stimulation.
source: This increase was found to be caused by Ca2+ influx through NIR-to-blue activated Opto-CRAC channels because cells incubated with the control NIR-to-green UCNPs (β-NaYF4: Yb, 2% Er @ β-NaYF4; emission maxima at 510 nm) did not show discernible changes in the GCaMP6s signal upon stimulation with the same NIR light (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated as experimental data with reference to a figure.

claim: NIR light remotely activated NFAT nuclear translocation at the cellular level.
source: We then employed NIR light to remotely activate the downstream effector NFAT at the cellular level, and observed NFAT nuclear translocation (Figure 3d), as well as NFAT-dependent IFN-γ production in CD4+ T lymphocytes (Figure 3f).
evidence: This is stated as experimental data with reference to figures.

claim: NIR light remotely activated NFAT-dependent IFN-γ production in CD4+ T lymphocytes.
source: We then employed NIR light to remotely activate the downstream effector NFAT at the cellular level, and observed NFAT nuclear translocation (Figure 3d), as well as NFAT-dependent IFN-γ production in CD4+ T lymphocytes (Figure 3f).
evidence: This is stated as experimental data with reference to figures.

claim: Luciferase-catalyzed bioluminescence was readily detected after NIR irradiation in mice implanted with HeLa cells expressing LOVSoc and NFAT-Luc pre-incubated with UCNPs-Stv.
source: Luciferase-catalyzed bioluminescence was readily detected after NIR irradiation, whereas no discernible background activation was observed in the negative controls where LOVSoc expression and/or NIR light were absent (Figure 3g).
evidence: This is stated as experimental data with reference to a figure.

claim: No discernible background activation was observed in negative controls where LOVSoc expression and/or NIR light were absent.
source: Luciferase-catalyzed bioluminescence was readily detected after NIR irradiation, whereas no discernible background activation was observed in the negative controls where LOVSoc expression and/or NIR light were absent (Figure 3g).
evidence: This is stated as experimental data with reference to a figure.

claim: Dendritic cells provide the essential link between the innate and adaptive immune responses.
source: Dendritic cells, which provide the essential link between the innate and adaptive immune responses, are adept at capturing tumor antigens and cross-presenting these antigens to T cells in tumor draining lymph nodes (dLNs), thereby sensitizing and generating tumor-specific cytotoxic lymphocytes (CTLs) to cause tumor regression or rejection (Palucka and Banchereau, 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: Dendritic cells are adept at capturing tumor antigens and cross-presenting these antigens to T cells in tumor draining lymph nodes.
source: Dendritic cells, which provide the essential link between the innate and adaptive immune responses, are adept at capturing tumor antigens and cross-presenting these antigens to T cells in tumor draining lymph nodes (dLNs), thereby sensitizing and generating tumor-specific cytotoxic lymphocytes (CTLs) to cause tumor regression or rejection (Palucka and Banchereau, 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: DC cross-presentation of tumor antigens sensitizes and generates tumor-specific cytotoxic lymphocytes to cause tumor regression or rejection.
source: Dendritic cells, which provide the essential link between the innate and adaptive immune responses, are adept at capturing tumor antigens and cross-presenting these antigens to T cells in tumor draining lymph nodes (dLNs), thereby sensitizing and generating tumor-specific cytotoxic lymphocytes (CTLs) to cause tumor regression or rejection (Palucka and Banchereau, 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: Pharmacological agents or signaling pathways controlling intracellular Ca2+ mobilization facilitate immature dendritic cell maturation through up-regulation of co-stimulatory molecules CD80 or CD86, MHC class I and class II, and CCR7.
source: Pharmacological agents (e.g., ionomycin) or signaling pathways controlling intracellular Ca2+ mobilization have been reported to facilitate immature dendritic cell maturation through up-regulation of co-stimulatory molecules CD80 or CD86, major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I and class II, as well as the chemokine receptor CCR7 (Félix et al., 2013; Matzner et al., 2008; Hsu et al., 2001; Koski et al., 1999; Czerniecki, 1997).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: NIR light stimulation resulted in approximately 2–8 fold increase in the surface expression of MHC-I/II, CD86, and CCR7 in bone marrow-derived DCs transduced with Opto-CRAC.
source: NIR light stimulation resulted in approximately 2–8 fold increase in the surface expression of MHC-I/II, CD86, and CCR7 (Figure 4b), which are characteristic of matured DCs that are capable of homing to dLNs to interact with T cells to modulate adaptive immune response (Palucka and Banchereau, 2012).
evidence: This is stated as experimental data with reference to a figure and citation.

claim: After NIR stimulation, co-cultured OT-1 CD8 T cells exhibited over 2-fold increase in both proliferation and IFN-γ release.
source: After NIR stimulation, co-cultured OT-1 CD8 T cells exhibited over 2-fold increase in both proliferation (Figure 4c) and IFN-γ release (Figure 4d), clearly attesting to the feasibility of using the NIR-stimulable Opto-CRAC system to expand and photo-prime antigen-specific T cells.
evidence: This is stated as experimental data with reference to figures.

claim: The proliferation of CD8 T cells was substantially up-regulated after NIR light stimulation in B16-OVA mice that received Opto-CRAC DCs.
source: Compared to the control group shielded from NIR, the proliferation of CD8 T cells was substantially up-regulated after light stimulation, by judging from decreased CFSE staining due to proliferative dilution and increased population of OT-1 CD8T cells in tumor draining LNs and spleens (Figure 4e).
evidence: This is stated as experimental data with reference to a figure.

claim: NIR light stimulation significantly suppressed tumor growth with diminished tumor volume in the B16-OVA melanoma model.
